title: add diacritic-insensitive search support
summary: ### Guidelines - [x] I have read the [guidelines to open issues](https://github.com/deckerst/aves/issues/234) ### Use case When searching through media files, albums, tags, or metadata that contain accented characters or diacritics (e.g., `é`, `è`, `à`, `ç`, `ö`, `ñ`), users currently need to enter the exact accented character to get relevant search results. If a search query is entered using standard ASCII characters (e.g., searching for `ete` instead of `été`, or `aeroport` instead of `aéroport`), matching items are not returned. ### Proposal Implement diacritic-insensitive (accent-insensitive) matching for search fields across the app (file names, tags, album names, metadata search, etc.). * Normalize both the search input string and target metadata strings (e.g., decomposing characters into base letters + combining diacritical marks via unicode normalization like `NFD` and stripping accents/diacritics). * Ensure that searching for `cafe` matches `café`, `CAFE`, and `café` seamlessly without requiring exact character accent matching. * ### Alternatives _No response_ ### Additional context Without diacritic-insensitive search, finding specific items quickly becomes exceptionally frustrating and tedious. Keyboard layouts on mobile devices often require long-pressing keys to select specific accented characters. When typing queries on the go, users naturally type plain ASCII letters expecting fuzzy or accent-agnostic matching. Having to switch keyboard layouts or meticulously long-press keys just to find a single photo or folder creates significant friction and drastically slows down everyday navigation within the app.
